title: NAT Terminology: Inside Local vs Inside Global

steps.objective: Enter privileged mode to explore NAT
steps.teachingPoint: In NAT, every device has TWO identities: what it calls itself (local) and what the Internet sees it as (global)!
Think of it like a secret agent: your REAL name (inside local) vs your COVER name (inside global).
INSIDE LOCAL = the server's REAL private IP (like 192.168.100.10) - what the server thinks its address is.
INSIDE GLOBAL = the server's PUBLIC IP (like 10.0.0.100) - what the Internet sees the server as.
When instructions say 'server should be known as x.x.x.100 on the outside' - they mean the INSIDE GLOBAL is x.x.x.100!

steps.objective: Enter LAN interface to see the inside network
steps.teachingPoint: CyberPatriot tip: 'x = match the outside network' means use the SAME network prefix as your WAN IP!
Example: If WAN is 10.0.0.34, and instructions say 'x.x.x.100', then inside global = 10.0.0.100
The static NAT command format: ip nat inside source static [INSIDE LOCAL] [INSIDE GLOBAL]
Real example: ip nat inside source static 192.168.100.10 10.0.0.100 (private server → public address)
